_README: Judgment inputs for the Risk tab. scripts/gen_risk_json.py reads this, joins it to
the live IBKR book (data/ibkr_flex.json) and live prices, and writes prototypes/risk.json.
EVERYTHING IN THIS FILE IS A HUMAN DECISION. Nothing here is refreshed by the pipeline.
The generator recomputes only what is unambiguously price-driven: marks, stop distances,
vol, ATR, touch probabilities, VaR, correlation, gross, stop_total and the budget meters.
Stops: an Activity Flex Query has 47 sections and none report working orders, so the
unattended pipeline cannot read a GTC stop. The IBKR MCP connector can, but only inside
a Claude session: scripts/ibkr_mcp_import.py turns that read into data/ibkr_live.json,
and while it is the fresher book gen_risk_json.py takes positions AND stops from it.
The stops below are the FALLBACK for runs that only have Flex - copy them from the
latest MCP read. A holding takes one `stop` plus the `qty` it was set against, or
`stops` as [{qty, stop}] tranches that must cover the whole position. Either way a
resized position is refused until its stops are re-read.
scenarios / slippage / gap are authored at the prices in price_basis against the
positions in basis_book. They do NOT auto-update - the betas behind rows other than
the gas shock are not documented, and the generator will not invent them. When live
prices drift past drift_tolerance, or the live book differs from basis_book, the
output carries judgment_stale=true and the tab says so. Re-derive them, update
basis_book and price_basis, and bump reviewed_on.
Derivations for the 27 Sep 2026 book (MSFT 200, SNOW 100, UNG 3,500), at the
2026-09-25 closes in price_basis, so every figure is reproducible:
Natural gas -20%: UNG at beta 1.0 to front-month gas. -20% takes UNG to 8.90, through
both stops, so clean fills = 1,500 x 0.48 + 2,000 x 1.78 = 4,280; gap = 38,955 x 0.20.
Mega-cap tech -10% / Enterprise software -10%: MSFT and SNOW at beta 1.0 to their own
theme. Both moves go through the stop, so clean fills = the stop distance.
Broad market -3%: OLS beta to SPX on simple daily returns, trailing 60 bars to
1.36, so the 60-bar figures are the conservative end - because the window holds
MSFT's +15.5% earnings day (30 Jul); without it MSFT's 60-bar beta is 1.07. Both
implied moves breach the stops. UNG's beta is -0.58 over 60 bars and -0.03 over 3
years: no hedge credit is taken for it, so UNG contributes nothing to this row.
Rates +50bp: 3-year regression of daily returns on daily ^TNX changes (n=756): MSFT
shows a loss when yields rise, none is significant, so the row carries no term. A
sample finding, not a claim of rate immunity - revisit after a real rate shock.
Gap cases (gaps): each name's own scenario move with the stop giving nothing - UNG -20%,
MSFT -10%, SNOW -10%. They are alternatives, not additive; each loads its own theme.
Removed: 'UNG realised drift, next 21d'. UNG's 60-bar mean return is -0.034%/day at
t -0.12, i.e. indistinguishable from zero, so a projected drift loss is noise.
Slippage: each UNG tranche fills x below its own stop, floored at the -20% gap price
(8.90) because a worse fill would be a larger shock than the row describes.
The earlier 369 energy term, -298 rates figure and -847 drift figure were never
documented and are replaced, not reverse-engineered.

news.title: Pipeline force majeure sends gas futures up 9% in a day
news.body: TC Energy's Columbia Gas Transmission declared force majeure on the Mountaineer XPress pipeline in West Virginia after a leak, cutting the segment to zero capacity from gas day 25 Sep - an estimated 1.4-1.8 Bcf/d. October NYMEX gas settled up 27.4 cents (+9.1%) at $3.297/MMBtu, its biggest one-day gain since January, then fell 15.1 cents (-4.6%) to $3.146 on 25 Sep, giving back about half the gain. UNG ended the week about 7% higher. Next EIA storage report: Thu 1 Oct.
news.src: Marcellus Drilling News, Energy News Beat, Reuters via BOE Report - Sep 2026

news.title: EIA: 53 Bcf injection, in line; surplus to five-year average narrows
news.body: For the week to 18 Sep the EIA reported a 53 Bcf net injection, matching the Reuters poll, taking working gas to 3,351 Bcf - 95 Bcf above the five-year average (down from 118 Bcf a week earlier) and 146 Bcf below a year ago.
news.src: EIA Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report, IndexBox - Sep 2026

news.title: Microsoft up 3.7% on Copilot relaunch; Oppenheimer lifts target
news.body: MSFT closed at $516.17 on 25 Sep, up 3.7% on the day and about 4.5% on the week. Coverage tied the move to Microsoft's Copilot relaunch (Home, Code, Autopilot), and Oppenheimer raised its price target to $570 the same day. The next earnings date is not yet confirmed by the company; calendars estimate late October - the 30 Jul report moved the stock 15.5% in a day, far more than the 4.9% cushion above the 491 stop.
news.src: Motley Fool, 24/7 Wall St, Wall Street Horizon - Sep 2026

news.title: Snowflake: no new catalyst since the 2 Sep beat
news.body: No confirmed company news in the fortnight; SNOW closed at $335.94 on 25 Sep, about 1% up on the week. The last report (2 Sep) showed product revenue of $1.491B, +37% year on year, and raised FY27 product revenue guidance to $6.07B.

notes: NAV is $300,000 throughout - the notional mandate assigned by the firm. Never measured against account equity, by instruction. 1% = $3,000.
Limits are provisional, set 15 Sep 2026: 2% maximum loss per theme, 6% across the portfolio. Not a written company risk policy.
Themes are assigned, not fed. IBKR returns no sector tags; every theme in this file is a stated assumption.

Stop distances are shown as probability of being touched over a holding period, not in daily sigma - these are GTC orders with no expiry. The probability is the reflection-principle first-passage estimate 2*Phi(-ln(S/B)/(sigma*sqrt(T))) on realised daily vol, zero drift.

Stops are the account's GTC working orders, read through the IBKR connector when the board is refreshed in session; the unattended daily run carries the last read forward, because an IBKR Activity Flex Query cannot report working orders. Where a position has more than one stop, the nearest one drives the touch probabilities and the dollar risk sums every tranche. Still unconfirmed: whether they are enabled outside regular trading hours - most gaps occur overnight, which is exactly when a stop is least likely to help.

Scenario betas: UNG ~1.0 to front-month gas; MSFT and SNOW 1.0 to their own theme; broad-market betas are measured 60-bar OLS (MSFT 1.81, SNOW 1.68) and are inflated by MSFT's 30 Jul earnings day - 1.07 without it. UNG's market beta is near zero to negative (-0.03 over 3 years), and no hedge credit is taken for it.

Scenario, slippage and gap figures are authored at the prices in price_basis against the positions in basis_book and do not move with the market. The tab flags them when prices drift past tolerance or the book changes.

Stops do not protect through a scheduled report. MSFT's next earnings (late October, unconfirmed) can gap it through 491: the 30 Jul report moved it 15.5% in a day, which downside would cost about $16.0k - 267% of the theme cap and 89% of the portfolio cap. The MSFT gap row uses the -10% scenario, so it is not the worst case.

Rates +50bp is not modelled for the book: no holding shows a significant yield sensitivity. The excluded TLT (900 shares) does - 3-year slope -0.137%/bp, t -52 - so +50bp would cost it about $4.9k, inside the same margin account.

Independently reviewed. The first issue (15 Sep 2026) was blocked and reissued: sigma framing replaced with touch probabilities, the -20% gas scenario corrected, and claims of a risk-free position and that the book was diversified withdrawn. The 27 Sep re-derivation was reviewed the same way; its findings (a buried gap breach, a missing MSFT gap case, a gas settle price, variance shares that ignored covariance) were fixed before publishing.

Stopped out: GOOGL and GNRC on 23 Sep, SMCI on 24 Sep, CRM on 25 Sep 2026. UNG was added to on 24 Sep (2,000 -> 3,500 shares) with a second stop on the new 1,500. MSFT and SNOW themes are assigned assumptions, not fed.
